payload.claim: The docstring says `verify` and `cite` each read the top layer's branch fresh, differing only in that one loads the policy and the other fetches. But `verify` (the `judge_verify` built from `_finish_verify`, used inside the `judge` closure a few lines below) never fetches the branch at all: it calls `package_phase.reverify` against the SHA already passed in (`top.head`), and `judge_draft` commits onto that SHA with no fetch. Only `cite` calls `package_phase.fetch_parent_branch` to get a fresh branch tip. This is exactly the asymmetry the spec's own 'Out of scope' notes describe as intentional (judge/verify reads the stale `top.head`, while `cite` reads the fetched tip that a review commit can move past), so the docstring's claim that both read the branch fresh contradicts both the code and the spec's own stated design.
